haiku: The paragraph mostly does not read machine-made. sonnet: The paragraph is built almost entirely from short, even questions and brief declaratives, so its rhythm is steady and list-like, with no digression, no concrete anecdote and no uneven sentence length. Each sentence makes one tidy point and then hands off to the next, so it reads as a polished outline of how a counselor would probe rather than one person thinking aloud.
